source_conclusions: Darwin helper captures contentView and refuses missing view before layer allocation; strong NSView.layer retains the borrowed descriptor pointer after local pool drainage. Production caller remains the serialized native main-thread construction callback.
Non-Darwin factory delegates to the prior wgpuglfw implementation. Normal surface/device teardown precedes GLFW view/window destruction.

Input callbacks, validation, retained state/copy/release, geometry sorting and malloc replies are byte-identical after stripping only pool wrappers and the added ownership comment. Nested geometry/publication pools retain accepted buffers before outer drainage.

Surface fixture uses counted NSObject stand-ins, nil-window/no-view refusal, replacements, caller-held ownership and final retirement; it avoids undocumented immediate CoreAnimation deallocation assumptions.
Swizzle original IMPs are captured before installing replacements; background factory calls use originals and do not mutate main-thread counters; original IMPs are restored in finally cleanup.

Input fixture checks completed_cycles separately from requested_cycles, accepted/refused publications, copied/retained geometry, caller-held data, caret, unmarked settlement and malloc reply lifetime.
limitations: This is a source-only internal review, not a qualification receipt; the reviewer ran no Go, Objective-C compilation, fixture binary, UI, GPU, provider or live test.
The headless layer fixture substitutes NSObject resources and does not prove actual CAMetalLayer, drawable, IOSurface, RSS or physical-footprint retirement.
Input admission callbacks are stubs and composition remains unmarked. This does not qualify human IME/preedit behavior or all diagnostic bridge paths.
Private factory assumes a valid nonnil GLFW object and native main-thread caller as guaranteed by current construction. Nil native window/contentView is refused by the C helper.
Previously measured native retention is a source-supported hypothesis; resolution requires a separately authorized quiet-host live campaign. No live run is currently authorized by this certificate.
